evidence: All three scored dimensions are mode='batched' with aggregation='weighted_mean', and each prompt explicitly instructs independent scoring with continuation after failure: functional/prompt.md:13 'Once it succeeds, score EACH criterion independently, continue after failures and keep successful observations. A failed sibling verdict is not evidence against another row. Shared protocols reduce setup; they are not conjunctive bundles. When a setup step fails, set up the same thing again on a new job of your own...'; polish/prompt.md:12 'Otherwise judge each criterion independently and continue after failures.'; visual/prompt.md:12 'Otherwise grade every criterion independently with its five anchors and continue after failures.' The shared 'Grading only' paragraph (line 7 in each) says give the failing criterion its lowest score '... and move on'. The NOT EXERCISED paragraph (functional:53, polish:18, visual:16) zeroes only 'the unobserved outcome' and says 'Preserve every completed independent observation.' No stop-on-first-failure wording exists in any scored prompt, judge.toml criterion text or app_context.md (grep for stop/abort/halt/first fail/remaining criteria returned nothing relevant). Cross-criterion references in criteria are anti-double-deduction ownership notes ('belongs to hro_bulk_places', 'graded only in hro_candidate_private'), and functional:23 'Never deduct one observed defect in more than one row'; functional:39 provides a fallback (Tomas's seeded Data Analyst conversation) so a failed hro_candidate_linked setup does not zero T/U/K rows. The only all-or-nothing rule in each scored prompt is the in-dimension global browser gate (functional:11-13, polish:11-12, visual:11-12), which mirrors the all_pass constraints gate hro_gate_shared and is the gate permitted by the template (template scored prompts likewise say the global gate is the only all-or-nothing rule). Gate dimensions render/constraints use aggregation='all_pass' and are exempt per the workbook. Counterexample attempts: (a) broken app that fails one early functional row (e.g. job creation with places validation) - other rows still scored because setup is re-created and verdicts are not inherited; a broken app cannot ride independence wording to extra credit because each row demands its own observation/control. (b) conforming app that could fail via coupling - only the gate couples rows, and an app passing the gate's job+candidate+observer readback is exactly the precondition the constraints gate already enforces, so no conforming app loses all rows to one unrelated miss.
notes: Source-wording check; it does not need runtime measurement to decide. No configured judge run exists (raw-evidence-index scope says so), so whether the GLM judge actually follows the independence instruction is not measured; that is not a row 38 defect. The private check-batched-independence-wording.py was not run; the manual reading finds the required wording in all three scored prompts. Out of scope for this row, for other reviewers: the in-dimension gate is stricter than the template's load/sign-in gate (it requires a server-backed create plus independent-context readback). It matches the constraints gate, so it adds no new coupling, but row 29/43 reviewers may want to check it. The task prompts also replace the template scored prompt text wholesale (e.g. the template functional 'Fail fast ... continue the rest' guardrail is gone, and equivalent wording sits at line 13); the template-preservation rows own that question.
